主要内容: The Federal Reserve issued Supervisory Letter SR 15-8 on June 25, 2015, outlining changes to the name check process for domestic and international applications. The letter states that the Fed will no longer consider whether an individual is 'known to banking' when determining if a name check is required. Instead, a completed name check will remain current for five years, and individuals or companies with current checks will generally not be rechecked unless circumstances suggest otherwise. The Fed will also use credit bureau reports in limited situations to supplement financial information provided in applications. These credit checks will be conducted on an ad hoc basis when relevant information from credit reports could aid the Fed's assessment. Questions about the policy should be directed to Susan Motyka, Patrick Grant, Katie Cox, or Betsy Howes-Bean. Institutions may also submit questions via the Board’s public website. The letter emphasizes that institutions must assess the appropriateness of initiating name checks beyond the scenarios specified in the letter. Name checks remain mandatory for all notifications under Regulation Y (12 CFR 225.72), unless an individual is exempt due to a recently completed name check, and there is no indication that a new check is necessary. The letter provides guidance on the procedures for conducting name checks and highlights the importance of ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements. Institutions are encouraged to review the letter to understand their obligations and ensure proper implementation of the name check process.
